what: Huntington Ingalls builds warships. It is the only American builder of nuclear aircraft carriers and one of two that build nuclear submarines, and it also does defence technology and services work.
customers: The United States Navy and Coast Guard, under long shipbuilding contracts.
money: aircraft carriers and Virginia and Columbia class submarines
unmanned systems, cyber and defence services
moat: The only dry docks in America that can build a nuclear aircraft carrier, and a workforce of shipbuilders that took generations to assemble. There is no second supplier.
risks: Shipbuilding margins have been squeezed by labour shortages and wage inflation on fixed-price contracts
A 4.9% net margin, and free cash flow of $327M is low against $13.5B of revenue
All revenue depends on Navy budgets and the pace of congressional appropriations
opportunities: 15.4 times earnings and analysts see about 25% upside, with 12 covering the stock
Revenue grew from $9.5B to $12.5B in four years and the backlog runs for years
Submarine production rates are being increased under the AUKUS agreement, which means more work for decades
watch: Shipbuilding operating margin and the submarine delivery schedule.
